items.text:
Posted this in the repo discussion for the inventory-count module since a few of us hit it during the warehouse audit last week.

The counting job runs fine for bin locations that have a single SKU, but as soon as a bin holds mixed lots it double-counts the remainder. I traced it to `reconcile_counts()` in `inventory/count.py` — it sums the quantity column before splitting by lot code, so lot A's leftover gets attributed to lot B as well. The AI assistant that reviews our PRs flagged the same function last month and suggested splitting on lot first, but nobody picked it up.

For now we work around it by exporting per-lot CSVs and merging them by hand, which defeats the point. Can someone own a fix before the next cycle? Suggested patch: group by `(bin_id, lot_code)` before the sum, then join back onto the expected table. Happy to write the test fixture if someone else does the code.

No rush on my account, but the audit sign-off is the 14th.

intent.requested_action: fix the double-counting bug in reconcile_counts before the next audit cycle

items.text: We've had a recurring problem in the library loan service: when a hold is placed on a title that's already checked out, the due-date reminder job keeps emailing the previous borrower after the item is returned and the hold is filled. The borrower gets three or four stale reminders and calls the desk confused. Our automated triage bot filed it under `loans/reminders` but never got assigned, so it just aged. I'm starting to think the reminder scheduler should re-check the loan status at send time instead of trusting the queue at enqueue time. Does anyone know if the `reminder_worker` reads from the same table the return handler writes to? If so the stale rows might be a simple cleanup-on-return. I can put together a repro with a seeded SQLite fixture if that helps whoever picks this up.

intent.requested_action: explain whether reminder_worker reads the same table as the return handler and possibly fix the stale reminders

items.text: Filed against the laptop refund flow, since the refund worker has been double-refunding partial returns. When a customer sends back only the charger, `refund_calc.py` computes the prorated amount on the full laptop price and then the webhook fires twice because the return event and the settlement event both trigger `issue_refund()`. We've seen three customers get paid above the order total. The coding assistant on our team earlier suggested idempotency keys keyed on the return ID; I think that's the right shape. Question for whoever owns this: is the settlement webhook supposed to be authoritative, or should `issue_refund()` refuse to pay out more than the captured amount regardless of caller? A hard ceiling plus idempotency would cover both bugs. I can add a fixture with a partial-return order and a duplicate settlement event if useful.

intent.requested_action: decide whether to make issue_refund enforce a payout ceiling and idempotency

items.text: Heads-up for anyone touching the library loan renewal endpoint: the grace-period override in `renewals.py` lets a patron renew past the max even when a hold is waiting, because it checks `hold_count` before applying the override instead of after. The assistant reviewing our changelog caught it and left a comment on the diff, which is how I found out. I'd argue the override should only apply when there are zero active holds, and the check should move below the override block. If nobody objects I'll flip the order and add a test with one active hold plus an active override and expect a 409. That should stop the front desk from having to cancel renewals by hand when a hold comes in. Ping me if you'd rather handle it in the branch you already have open.

intent.requested_action: review the proposed renewal override fix and reply if they want to handle it
